title: TRUMP POSTS A 15-POINT GAZA PLAN; NETANYAHU REPLIES WITH POINT 16: NO
kicker: A U.S. Gaza proposal meets Israeli rejection, so the fictional leaders’ chat turns into a negotiation over what the word ‘plan’ was supposed to mean.
summary: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu rejected the U.S. 15-point Gaza plan and said Israeli forces would not withdraw until Hamas disarms, according to reporting from BBC News, Al Jazeera and The Guardian.

sources.label: Israel rejects Trump’s 15-point plan for Gaza
Israel rejects Trump's 15-point plan for Gaza, Netanyahu says
Middle East crisis live: Netanyahu rejects US’s Gaza plan and vows no withdrawal until Hamas disarms

messages.speaker: UN Admin
messages.text: New thread: Gaza plan. Facts and public statements are sourced; the private replies below are fictional satire.

messages.speaker: Trump
messages.text: Fifteen points. Very complete. People love numbered plans because you can tell they have points.

messages.speaker: Netanyahu
messages.text: I read all fifteen. I have notes. The first note is no withdrawal before disarmament.

messages.speaker: Macron
messages.text: A plan is not yet an agreement. Europe has several binders proving this.

messages.speaker: Meloni
messages.text: Can we get one geopolitical document where the word ‘final’ survives contact with the participants?

messages.speaker: Xi
messages.text: China notes that numbered plans have a tendency to acquire additional points after publication.

editorial.reviewNotes: Merged three reports covering the same Gaza-plan rejection into one event. S-M-A-R review keeps the satire focused on leaders and negotiation dynamics, not civilians.

messages.text: New rule: shipping-lane arguments go in #maritime-chaos.

messages.text: Some vessels may require… premium access.

title: AMERICA CLOSES CONSULATES; CHINA REPLIES “THANKS FOR THE OPEN DESK SPACE”
kicker: Diplomatic cost-cutting becomes a fictional real-estate argument over who occupies the influence left behind.
summary: The move aims to protect US firms as they face increasing competition from China's chip industry.

article.headline: AMERICA CLOSES CONSULATES; CHINA REPLIES “THANKS FOR THE OPEN DESK SPACE”
article.dek: The technology is real and consequential. The comedy is watching founders, regulators and governments all claim they are the responsible adult in the room.
body: The move aims to protect US firms as they face increasing competition from China's chip industry.

The original reporting points to one factual conclusion. This version keeps that conclusion intact and leaves the public choreography visible: who is claiming credit, who is objecting and which part of the official language is doing the most work.
The technology is real and consequential. The comedy is watching founders, regulators and governments all claim they are the responsible adult in the room.
The conversation below is the imagined off-mic layer. It exaggerates recognizable reactions and rivalries, but it does not change the event, outcome or source record.
article.sourceCredit: Based on original reporting from BBC News. Open the source links for the full reporting.

messages.text: Diplomatic footprint changes detected. Please stop calling embassies retail locations.

messages.speaker: Trump
messages.text: We are cutting waste. Very efficient.

messages.speaker: Xi
messages.text: Efficiency is admirable. We will efficiently schedule some meetings nearby.

messages.speaker: Macron
messages.text: Influence has a curious habit of occupying vacant offices.

messages.speaker: Meloni
messages.text: You cannot cancel diplomacy like a streaming subscription and act surprised when the plot continues.

messages.speaker: Milei
messages.text: Have you considered replacing every consulate with a chainsaw emoji? Asking academically.

messages.text: Nobody is giving China our desks. We are simply not using the desks.

messages.speaker: Xi
messages.text: That distinction is extremely convenient for the person interested in the desks.

messages.speaker: Macron
messages.text: Diplomatic influence is not furniture, although apparently we are testing the theory.

messages.speaker: Meloni
messages.text: Please tell me nobody put ‘soft power’ on Facebook Marketplace.

messages.speaker: Trump
messages.text: If we did, we would get a fantastic price.

messages.speaker: Xi
messages.text: China has saved the listing.
